concept: Timeline prints a log of things that already happened, the way a device prints its last events on a tape: the time in a column at the left, a hairline of ink down the case, and a small node on the line where each event meets it. It reports the past and does nothing else.

default_to_avoid.pattern: timeline of coloured icon discs on a thick coloured line with a card for each event
default_to_avoid.why_not: Coloured discs tell the kind of event by colour alone and look like keys that can be pressed, and a card around every event turns a log into a pile of boxes.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Timeline copied from Stepper with numbered windows and a dotted rail
default_to_avoid.why_not: A Stepper counts sections still to come; a log has no numbers, so the time is printed and the line is solid ink.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): figures printed in a fixed column beside the keys
Schematic faces of Braun audio gear: a hairline joins parts and a small node marks where it meets one
system/CONCEPT.md P8 Relations are drawn: lines run between the parts they join with a node at each part

derivation.consequence: a relation is a hairline of ink with a small node where it meets a part
derivation.form: The rail is a one-pixel hairline in ring ink and each event has a small ring node on it, so the line joins the events in order.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: The time is printed in tabular figures in a fixed column, so the minutes of every event line up under each other.

derivation.consequence: the chosen word carries one ink index mark beside it
derivation.form: The latest event is the one lit entry: its node is filled with ink and its title turns medium, and the rest stay plain rings.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The node, the line and the text are all ink, so a log never takes the unit's one orange.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation
derivation.form: Events are printed in place and nothing slides in or fades, so a log that grows adds a row and moves nothing else.

options.name: time column with a hairline rail and nodes
tape with ticks and the time above

variants.reason: A follows P8, a hairline with a node where it meets a part, and keeps the times in one aligned column; B repeats the recessed window of Stepper and Input so the times look like fields, and C reads as a block quote with a ruler and breaks the time column.

root.why: An ordered list, one row per event in the order given, so the order is read out and positions do not reflow when an event is added.

item.why: An event holds its time, rail and text in a three-column grid so every time, node and title shares one column.

time.why: The time is a time element in the label size and secondary ink with tabular figures, right-aligned to the rail.

rail.why: The column that holds the hairline; it runs to the next event and stops after the last one.

node.why: A small ring where the hairline meets an event, level with the first line of its title; the lit event's node carries the word Latest as its label.

content.why: The column that holds the title and detail, with a gap under it so the next event starts one clear step down.

title.why: The event's name in the body size in primary ink, level with the first line of the row; the lit event turns it medium.

detail.why: Optional text under the title in secondary ink, aligned to the title's left edge so the log reads down one line.

data-latest.why: The node fills with ink and the title turns medium, and the node is read out as Latest, so the lit entry is a shape, a weight and a word, not a colour.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the hairline and the node draw in the text colour and the filled node stays filled.
